raw_case_text:
In May 2023, a 63-year-old man presented with a fever peaking at 38 C, chills, fatigue, and poor overall well-being. Laboratory results indicated erythrocytopenia, with red blood cell (RBC) count at 2.2x1012/L, hemoglobin (Hb) at 72g/L, and platelet count (PLT) at 80x109/L; reticulocyte percentage was notably high at 9.7%. Elevated levels of C-reactive protein (CRP) at 63.6mg/L, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) at 80mm/h, ferritin at 1469ng/mL, and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) at 1103U/L were observed (Table 1). The patient tested positive for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) IgM, with both urine occult blood and hemosiderin tests returning positive results. Ultrasonography revealed splenomegaly. A bone marrow biopsy indicated active hyperplasia, with a decreased granulocyte to nucleated erythrocyte ratio, and erythroid hyperplasia being predominant, featuring occasionally hemophagocytic cells. Initially treated for hemophagocytic syndrome induced by EBV infection, the patient received ciprofloxacin, cyclosporine, dexamethasone, and etoposide in local hospital. Despite some improvement, weakness persisted.
In July 2023, the patient was readmitted with a low-grade fever. Routine laboratory tests revealed the following: RBC count at 1.58x1012/L, Hb level at 61g/L, PLT count at 76x109/L, Reticulocyte percentage at 15.71%, CRP count at 19.6mg/L, ESR at 66mm/h, Serum total bilirubin at 35.0mumol/L, Serum direct total bilirubin at 22.4mumol/L, and blood EBV DNA at 5.26x103 copies /mL (Table 1). A chest CT scan identified scattered nodules across both lungs, with a notably larger one located in the lower right lung (Figure 1A). Bone marrow smear analysis indicated that phagocytic reticulum cells constituted 0.5%, while the bone marrow biopsy did not reveal any abnormal cells. PET-CT showed that the metabolism of Fluoro-Deoxy-Glucose (FDG) in bone marrow cavity was slightly increased, and the spleen was full with FDG metabolism. Although lymphoma could not be entirely ruled out based on the existing diagnostic evidence, the primary concern was hemolytic anemia in conjunction with the confirmed EBV infection. Consequently, the patient received treatment with dexamethasone and cyclosporine to manage the hemolytic condition, in addition to galiximab, before being discharged. 
In September 2023, the patient was rehospitalized due to an exacerbation of symptoms, including a severe cough with sputum production, chest tightness, and acute shortness of breath following physical activity. Laboratory investigations showed RBC count of 1.81x1012/L; Hb level at 63g/L; PLT count at 206x109/L; Reticulocyte percentage at 15.8%; CRP level at 76.2mg/L and ESR at 99mm/h (Table 1). A CT scan of the lungs revealed a new mass in the upper lobe of the right lung (Figure 1B). Tests for fungal and bacterial infections, including fungal culture, bacterial culture, TB smear, Cryptococcus neoformans capsular antigen, Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA, respiratory virus screening, and fungal immunofluorescence staining, returned negative results. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of sputum identified Babesia microti, Nocardia cyriacigeorgica, Pneumocystis yersii, and human herpesvirus. Additional mNGS testing of alveolar lavage fluid and blood samples also detected Babesia microti (Figure 2). Examination of a peripheral blood Giemsa smear showed 27.9% parasitaemia with Babesia microti (Figure 3).  
Upon inquiring about the patient's history of exposure, it was discovered that the patient had been bitten on the neck by ticks six months earlier while working in a mountainous area, though no significant bite marks or lesions were observed, and no treatment had been administered at that time. Treatment was initiated with atovaquone 750 mg orally Q12h plus azithromycin 500 mg intravenous injection Q24h for Babesia, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim for Pneumocystis jirovecii and Nocardia, along with human immunoglobulin to bolster immunity. Following this regimen, the chest CT scan in November 2023 and routine laboratory tests in January 2024 both showed that the patient had recovered.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 63-year-old man treated with dexamethasone, cyclosporine, and etoposide for suspected EBV-associated hemophagocytic syndrome and hemolytic anemia presented in September 2023 with severe productive cough, chest tightness, and acute exertional shortness of breath.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In May 2023, the patient initially presented with fever up to 38 °C, chills, fatigue, hemolytic anemia (Hb 72 g/L, reticulocytes 9.7%), thrombocytopenia (80 x 10^9/L), hyperferritinemia (1,469 ng/mL), elevated LDH (1,103 U/L), splenomegaly, positive EBV IgM, and erythroid hyperplasia with occasional hemophagocytosis on bone marrow biopsy; he was treated at a local hospital for presumed EBV-induced hemophagocytic syndrome with ciprofloxacin, cyclosporine, dexamethasone, and etoposide. In July 2023, he was readmitted with low-grade fever, persistent hemolytic anemia (Hb 61 g/L, reticulocytes 15.71%, total bilirubin 35.0 μmol/L, direct bilirubin 22.4 μmol/L), EBV DNAemia (5.26 x 10^3 copies/mL), and scattered bilateral lung nodules on chest CT (largest in the right lower lobe), and received dexamethasone, cyclosporine, and galiximab. In September 2023, he was rehospitalized for acute exacerbation of severe productive cough, chest tightness, and exertional dyspnea. Retrospective exposure history revealed he had been bitten on the neck by ticks 6 months earlier while working in a mountainous area.
subjective.past_medical_history: Presumed EBV-associated hemophagocytic syndrome and Coombs/hemolytic anemia diagnosed in May 2023, treated with dexamethasone, cyclosporine, etoposide, and galiximab; occupational tick bite on the neck 6 months prior while working in a mountainous area.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, fatigue, severe cough with sputum production, chest tightness, and acute exertional dyspnea.

objective.physical_examination: Splenomegaly noted on baseline evaluation; febrile up to 38 °C at initial onset.
objective.routine_investigations: May 2023 labs: RBC 2.2 x 10^12/L, Hb 72 g/L, PLT 80 x 10^9/L, reticulocytes 9.7%, CRP 63.6 mg/L, ESR 80 mm/h, ferritin 1,469 ng/mL, LDH 1,103 U/L, positive EBV IgM, positive urine occult blood and hemosiderin; abdominal ultrasound showed splenomegaly. July 2023 labs: RBC 1.58 x 10^12/L, Hb 61 g/L, PLT 76 x 10^9/L, reticulocytes 15.71%, CRP 19.6 mg/L, ESR 66 mm/h, total bilirubin 35.0 μmol/L, direct bilirubin 22.4 μmol/L, blood EBV DNA 5.26 x 10^3 copies/mL. September 2023 admission labs: RBC 1.81 x 10^12/L, Hb 63 g/L, PLT 206 x 10^9/L, reticulocytes 15.8%, CRP 76.2 mg/L, ESR 99 mm/h; negative routine bacterial/fungal cultures, TB smear, MTB DNA, Cryptococcus capsular antigen, respiratory virus panel, and fungal immunofluorescence staining. Peripheral blood Giemsa-stained smear (September 2023): Intraerythrocytic Babesia microti parasites with 27.9% parasitemia.
objective.advanced_workup: May & July 2023 bone marrow biopsies and PET-CT: Active erythroid hyperplasia with occasional hemophagocytic cells (0.5% phagocytic reticulum cells) and increased bone marrow and splenic 18F-FDG uptake on PET-CT without overt lymphoma. Serial chest CT scans: Scattered bilateral pulmonary nodules with a larger right lower lobe nodule in July 2023, followed by a new mass in the right upper lobe in September 2023. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) in September 2023: Sputum mNGS identified Babesia microti, Nocardia cyriacigeorgica, Pneumocystis jirovecii ('Pneumocystis yersii'), and human herpesvirus; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and peripheral blood mNGS both confirmed Babesia microti.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Severe human babesiosis (Babesia microti with 27.9% parasitemia on Giemsa blood smear and positive blood/BALF/sputum mNGS—which had initially mimicked EBV-induced hemophagocytic syndrome and autoimmune hemolytic anemia following a mountain tick bite) complicated by immunosuppression-induced pulmonary co-infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii, Nocardia cyriacigeorgica, and human herpesvirus (confirmed by sputum mNGS and right upper lobe mass on chest CT). Plan and clinical course: Treated with oral atovaquone (750 mg q12h) plus intravenous azithromycin (500 mg q24h) for Babesia microti, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) for Pneumocystis jirovecii and Nocardia cyriacigeorgica, and intravenous human immunoglobulin. Follow-up chest CT in November 2023 and routine hematologic/biochemical tests in January 2024 confirmed complete clinical, hematologic, and radiographic recovery.
